title: High quality DNA extraction protocol from recalcitrant plant tissues
author: Todd GB McLay
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i8jchun

steps.title: Stir until clear
steps.instruction: Mix the solution on an unheated stir plate until it becomes clear.

steps.title: Prepare 100x BSA and NaCl mix
steps.instruction: Make 100 × (=4 %) BSA by dissolving BSA powder in water. Combine this 100 × BSA with 5 M NaCl at a 5 : 1 ratio (NaCl : BSA). Store the mixture frozen for long‑term use.

steps.title: Prepare CTAB solution with additives
steps.instruction: Add 600 mL of CTAB per sample to a Falcon tube. In a fume hood, add 2 µL of β‑mercaptoethanol (BME) per mL of CTAB and 4 µL of Proteinase K per reaction. Warm the mixture at 65 °C.

steps.title: Grind tissue and label tubes
steps.instruction: Grind 20–50 mg of plant tissue (e.g., with liquid nitrogen and grinding sand). Transfer the ground tissue into a labelled 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube and label two additional tubes per sample (now or later).

steps.title: Add STE, vortex, and spin
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of STE to the tissue, vortex thoroughly, then spin at 5 000 rpm for 10 min. Discard the supernatant by pouring it off.

steps.title: Add CTAB & NaCl:BSA, incubate
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, add 500 µL of the pre‑warmed CTAB solution to each tube, then add 100 µL of the NaCl:BSA solution. Vortex, and incubate at 65 °C for at least 1 hour (up to overnight), vortexing or shaking several times during incubation.

steps.title: Chloroform extraction and centrifugation
steps.instruction: Add 450 µL of chloroform to each tube. If the volume does not fit, split the tissue‑CTAB mixture into two Eppendorf tubes and add 450 µL chloroform to each. Shake to mix, open the tube briefly with a kimwipe to release gas, then centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 min.

steps.title: Recover aqueous phase and second extraction
steps.instruction: Using a P200 pipette set to 190 µL, transfer the top aqueous phase (≈300–400 µL) to a new Eppendorf tube, avoiding the solid layer. Add 450 µL of chloroform to this aqueous phase, shake, vent with a kimwipe, and centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 min. Again using the P200 set to 190 µL, transfer the top aqueous phase (≈300–400 µL) to a new tube.

steps.title: Isopropanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of room‑temperature isopropanol to the aqueous phase and mix by gently inverting five times. OPTIONAL: add 110 µL of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) before the isopropanol, then incubate at room temperature for 20 min. (Note: this optional step failed for some taxa.)

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 min with tubes facing inwards (hinge outward). A DNA pellet may form at the tube bottom; carefully pour off the supernatant.

steps.title: Ethanol wash and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of freshly prepared 70 % ethanol, dislodge the pellet by pipetting or flicking, then centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 min. Carefully pour off the ethanol.

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Leave the tubes open on the bench or in a fume hood (cover with kimwipes) to dry the pellet for at least 2 hours up to overnight.

steps.title: Resuspend in Tris‑HCl (first)
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8, to the dried pellet and allow the DNA to resuspend for at least 1 hour before use.

steps.title: Sodium acetate ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 100 % ethanol and 36.25 µL of 2.4 M sodium acetate to each tube, mix by inverting, and centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 min. (This step can be merged with the isopropanol step by adding NaAcetate to reach a final concentration of 0.3 M, though it failed for Xanthorrhoea.)

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Pour off the supernatant, add 1 000 µL of 70 % ethanol, dislodge the pellet by pipetting or flicking, and centrifuge at maximum speed for 3 min.

steps.title: Final air‑dry
steps.instruction: Carefully pour off the supernatant and dry the pellet for at least 2 hours up to overnight with tubes open and kimwipes covering them.

steps.title: Final resuspension and QC
steps.instruction: Add 50–100 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8, allow the DNA to resuspend for at least 1 hour, then assess quality and quantity using spectrophotometry.
